items.title: Why embargoes matter for open source security
items.text: Open source is built on a foundation of transparency, collaboration, and speed. We share code, we share ideas, and together, we build better software. But when it comes to discovering and patching security vulnerabilities, that standard model of immediate, public sharing has to temporarily shift. A security embargo is a temporary agreement to keep a software vulnerability private so that vendors and maintainers can create and release a security patch before malicious actors learn how to exploit

items.title: Protect your Launchpad API tokens with a security key
items.text: Supply-chain attacks that harvest developer credentials are on the rise. The Shai-Hulud campaign, for example, used automated scanners to sweep up any secrets they could find in files and keyrings. If you use Launchpad’s API, one of those secrets is your API token – and until now it has been about as safe as the laptop it sits on. This release is a Regular release and as such, it is supported for 9 months, until July 2026. Since it’s just out, you may experience some issues,... Continue reading

items.title: Ubuntu Studio 25.10 Beta Released
items.text: The Ubuntu Studio team is pleased to announce the beta release of Ubuntu Studio 25.10, codenamed “Questing Quokka”. items.title: Ubuntu Studio 24.04.3 LTS Released
items.text: The Ubuntu Studio team is pleased to announce the release of Ubuntu Studio 24.04.3 LTS. This is a minor release which wraps-up the security and bug fixes into one .iso image, available for download now.
